items.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001
items.q: I’ll tell you Ellington wasn’t the greatest reader, did you know that?

ctx.x: I have not got the capability to study like other guys. It has to be by osmosis or just some other way. And there’s plenty of my friends that work that way that have turned out great music that don’t read well and haven’t studied a lot but write so beautifully. And there might be something to acknowledge that if a person doesn’t have the usual skills, don’t count him out. He might have something else going on that is/are unusual because they aren’t the usual. And in my experience some of my favorite musicians…

reading skills or orchestrating skills, had to pick it up in their own way and have contributed maybe more than anybody else. So there’s something — I’ll tell you Ellington wasn’t the greatest reader, did you know that?

items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We were on tour together. They put the sidemen in one big room and the leaders, Duke and I, in a separate room.

ctx.x: Then Balboa Ballroom, maybe, where he really started getting an audience, which is a very strange thing, that he was almost – he was planning to break up, and a turnaround, because that audience in Denver really liked him, and then later on, in California. But there were always bands coming through. It wasn’t an isolated place, by no means. The way I heard, or met, Duke for the first time: he was playing in Stockton, and I went. Jimmy Branford [sic: Blanton] had passed away. He was on the West Coast, and he…

wonderful.” I told him how much I thought of Ellington, the records I had from the ’30s, like Warm Valley, Flaming Sword, Jack the Bear, which has that wonderful bass solo on it. He said, “You’re an Ellington fan. Would you like to meet Duke?” I said, “Oh yes.” He said, “He’s right in this dressing room over here. Let me bring you over.” He knocked on the door and went in. I followed him. He introduced me. Duke looked up at me. I couldn’t open my mouth. I couldn’t say a word. I said to myself, this is ridiculous.…
So he didn’t travel out of a suitcase.
